queries.hook: A mind that will not settle, running through the night and landing on the phone, with no quiet minute to rest.
queries.diagnose: The untrained mind runs like the wind, replaying and imagining; left to itself it becomes its own enemy, and the phone gives it no rest.
queries.steady: Praise and blame, gain and loss, pleasure and pain come and go; the one who stays the same in the middle of it is the one who is free.
queries.act: Practise one quiet minute before the phone; let the mind land on one thing and rest there, even for a minute.

verse.speaker: Arjuna
verse.setting: Arjuna confesses the mind is as hard to hold as the wind; Krishna answers.
verse.sanskrit: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम् । तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् ॥
verse.line: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.
verse.translation: For the mind is restless, Krishna, turbulent, powerful and stubborn. I think it is as hard to hold as the wind.
verse.why: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

prasang.title: Mastering the mind
prasang.summary: Arjuna says the mind is restless, stormy and stubborn. Krishna agrees, and says practice and letting go can train it.
prasang.lesson: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

verse.meaning: Arjuna is looking at their own mind and telling Krishna that it is impossible to control. The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. It is as hard to hold as the wind. Krishna hears this and does not argue. He simply says that the mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go can train it.
verse.for_you: Your mind is restless right now. It is not weak. It is strong and stubborn, like the wind. To hold it, you do not need to force it. You could practice letting it go.

verse.speaker: Rama
verse.setting: Rama describes his restless mind to the sages.
verse.sanskrit: चेतः पतति कार्येषु विहगः स्वामिषेष्विव । क्षणेन विरतिं याति बालः क्रीडनकादिव ॥
verse.line: The mind pounces on a task like a bird on food, then drops it like a bored child's toy.
verse.translation: The mind swoops onto tasks like a bird onto meat, and a moment later loses interest, like a child with a toy.
verse.why: Naming honestly what feels empty is the first step; Rama's lament is a question, not the answer.

prasang.title: Rama's lament: what is the point of all this?
prasang.summary: Asked to speak, Rama pours out what he has seen: wealth hardens people, life drips away like water off a leaf, ego and craving run us, the mind never fills, childhood, youth and old age each bring their own suffering, and time eats everything. He ends by saying only the company of good people gives him hope.
prasang.story_hook: In front of the whole court, the young prince stood up and said what everyone feels and nobody says.
prasang.lesson: Naming honestly what feels empty is the first step; Rama's lament is a question, not the answer.

verse.meaning: Rama is sitting with the sages and speaking plainly. He tells them his mind is a problem. It is restless, stormy, and stubborn. He says it is like trying to hold the wind. The mind does not stay still. It moves from one thing to the next without rest.
verse.for_you: The seven hours on the phone are not the only thing here. Your mind is doing the same thing. It moves from one thing to the next and never settles. This is what Rama is naming, and it is the first truth you could see.

verse.speaker: Yama
verse.sanskrit: यस्त्वविज्ञानवान्भवत्ययुक्तेन मनसा सदा । तस्येन्द्रियाण्यवश्यानि दुष्टाश्वा इव सारथेः ॥ यस्तु विज्ञानवान्भवति युक्तेन मनसा सदा । तस्येन्द्रियाणि वश्यानि सदश्वा इव सारथेः ॥
verse.line: Without understanding, the senses bolt like wild horses; with a steady mind, they run like trained ones.
verse.translation: For one who lacks understanding, whose mind is never held steady, the senses run out of control like a driver's wild horses. For one who has understanding, whose mind is always steady, the senses obey like good horses.
verse.why: Hold the reins of your mind, or your senses will drive for you.

prasang.title: The chariot of the self
prasang.summary: Yama pictures a person as a chariot: the self is the rider, the body the chariot, the intellect the driver, the mind the reins and the senses the horses. With a steady mind the horses obey; without it they bolt. He ends with the call to arise and wake.
prasang.lesson: Hold the reins of your mind, or your senses will drive for you.

verse.meaning: Yama speaks to Nachiketa about the chariot of the self. He says that without understanding, the senses bolt like wild horses. With a steady mind, they run like trained ones. He is explaining that the mind is the reins. If you do not hold the reins, the horses will run where they want. If you hold them, they go where you intend.
verse.for_you: The phone is a wild horse. It moves your mind wherever the screen lights up. You can hold the reins. Pick one task and let your eyes rest on it until it is done. Let the rest wait.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to the grieving Arjuna, on what in us is never born and never dies.
verse.sanskrit: यं हि न व्यथयन्त्येते पुरुषं पुरुषर्षभ । समदुःखसुखं धीरं सोऽमृतत्वाय कल्पते ॥
verse.line: The one who stays the same in pain and pleasure, undisturbed by either, is ready for real freedom.
verse.translation: The steady person whom these do not disturb, who stays the same in pain and pleasure, becomes fit for immortality.
verse.why: What you truly are outlasts every loss and every passing pain.
verse.misuse: Steadiness is not numbness or hiding what you feel.

prasang.title: The teaching of the deathless Self (Sankhya)
prasang.summary: Krishna begins his teaching: the self is eternal, bodies change like clothes, and pleasure and pain come and go. Grief for what must pass should not overwhelm us.
prasang.lesson: What you truly are outlasts every loss and every passing pain.

verse.meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna that the person who can stand in the middle of pain and pleasure without being thrown off balance is the one who is ready to be free. This is not about being cold or not feeling anything. It is about not letting a single feeling take over the whole person. When joy comes, it is known as joy. When pain comes, it is known as pain. Neither one is allowed to become the whole story.
verse.for_you: When the restlessness comes, let it be there as restlessness. Do not let it become the whole of who you are. You are the one who notices the restlessness, and that is a different thing entirely.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna teaches Arjuna how to meditate and what a settled mind is like.
verse.sanskrit: यतो यतो निश्चरति मनश्चञ्चलमस्थिरम् । ततस्ततो नियम्यैतदात्मन्येव वशं नयेत् ॥
verse.line: Wherever the restless mind wanders, gently bring it back. Again and again.
verse.translation: Wherever the restless, unsteady mind wanders, from there one should draw it back and bring it under the control of the self.
verse.why: Moderation and gentle return, again and again, settle the mind.

prasang.title: Meditation in detail
prasang.summary: Krishna describes meditation: moderation in food and sleep, the mind like a lamp in a windless place, bringing the wandering mind back, and feeling others' joy and pain as one's own.
prasang.lesson: Moderation and gentle return, again and again, settle the mind.

verse.meaning: Krishna is showing Arjuna how to sit with the mind when it wants to run. The mind is not a wild animal that must be beaten into place. It is a restless thing that will look at a hundred different directions in one minute. The teaching is not to fight it. It is to notice where it has gone and to turn it back, gently, again and again. This is the whole practice. The mind does not need to be fixed in one day.
verse.for_you: Before you pick up the phone, sit for one quiet minute. When the mind wanders to the screen or the noise, notice it. Then bring it back to the feeling of your own breathing. Do this one more time. That is the practice for today.

verse.setting: After the war, Lakshmana finds Rama alone and asks how to cross the sea of confusion.

verse.translation: Sitting in a quiet place, senses at rest, self-mastered, pure within, one should contemplate the One with undivided attention, resting in the Self.
verse.why: Quiet sitting and steady faith carry you until understanding becomes natural.

prasang.title: Sit quietly, keep faith
prasang.summary: Rama describes sitting in a quiet place with the senses at rest until the mind becomes like a still ocean, and tells Lakshmana that until he sees the divine everywhere, devotion keeps it alive in the heart.
prasang.lesson: Quiet sitting and steady faith carry you until understanding becomes natural.

verse.meaning: After the war, Lakshmana finds Rama alone and asks how to cross the sea of confusion. Rama tells him to sit somewhere quiet, let the senses rest, and give your full attention to one thing. This is not about emptying the mind or fighting the noise. It is about finding a place where the senses can rest, and directing the full attention to one object. In that quiet space, steady faith carries you until understanding becomes natural.
verse.for_you: Before you reach for the phone tomorrow morning, try sitting in one quiet spot for a single minute. Let your eyes rest, and give your full attention to the sound of your own breath. This is the first quiet minute before the noise begins again.

story.title: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
story.story_hook: One spring morning, a king out for a walk overheard a song that he could not stop thinking about.
story.summary: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind that no longer clutches.
story.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

anchor.speaker: Janaka
anchor.setting: King Janaka, alone on his palace roof after overhearing wandering sages, rethinks his life.
anchor.sanskrit: संपदश्च विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेच्चित्तेन संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा हन्त मन्ये महापदः ॥ आपदोऽपि विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेन्मनसि संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा मन्ये मनसि संपदः ॥
anchor.line: Good fortune the mind clutches becomes trouble. Trouble the mind accepts becomes a kind of fortune.
anchor.translation: All those dazzling fortunes, if the mind clings to them, are really great calamities in grand disguise. And all those varied misfortunes, if the mind accepts them, are really fortunes.
anchor.why: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.
anchor.misuse: Accepting a hardship doesn't mean not fixing what can be fixed.

script: You are carrying a mind that will not settle. It is scattered, and the seven hours a day on your phone are not helping it land. You feel the stress of it, but you do not know how to bring it to a stop.
Arjuna tells Krishna that the mind is impossible to control. Arjuna said:
चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम्, तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम्.
In plain words: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.

The mind is not weak. It is strong and stubborn, like the wind. Holding it by force is exhausting because it is not meant to be grasped. What can train it is practice and letting go. This is easier said than done because every notification asks for your attention, and every habit wants to be repeated. But the truth underneath is that the mind can be trained without a fight.

When you feel the restlessness rising, try letting go for one minute. Put the phone face down and simply notice your breath. Do not try to fix the thoughts. Just let them be there and let your attention rest on one thing.
What would happen if you let the wind move for just one minute?

depth.life: You are under twenty-five and studying. Your mind will not settle, and your phone sits in your hand for seven hours a day. The voice note you sent was vague and hesitant, and you feel stressed and scattered.
depth.points: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. It is not weak. It is powerful, and trying to force it only makes it fight back. The practice is not to grab it, but to let it go and return.
depth.practice: Set a timer for ten minutes and put the phone face down. Let your mind wander without touching the screen, and notice what comes up.
depth.question: What happens in your chest when you put the phone down and do nothing?
